questions.q: What are the four main branches of science mentioned in the chapter, and what is the primary focus of Physics?
questions.a: The four branches are Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Earth Science. Physics focuses on matter, energy, and fundamental forces, such as motion and gravity. A wrong answer here suggests the student has not yet distinguished between the "what" (matter) and the "how" (forces) of nature.

questions.q: If you are studying why ice melts into water when heated, which branch of science would this primarily fall under and why?
questions.a: This falls under Chemistry, because it involves a change in the state of a substance. Students who say "Biology" are likely confusing "nature" with "living things," failing to distinguish between chemical properties and biological life functions.

questions.q: A scientist is tracking the path of a planet through the solar system. Which branch of science is this, and how does it relate to the branch that studies the Earth?
questions.a: This is Astronomy. It relates to Earth Science because both study large-scale systems (planets/stars vs. rocks/oceans). A wrong answer here shows the student does not see the connection between the "Earth system" and the "Universe system."

questions.q: Compare the study of a forest (Biology) with the study of the rocks beneath it (Earth Science). How are these two branches connected in a real-world environment?
questions.a: They are connected because the rocks provide the soil and nutrients that the living organisms in the forest need to survive. A student who says they are "completely unrelated" fails to understand that all branches of science overlap in the real world.

questions.q: "Science is just about memorizing the names of the branches." Is this statement true or false? Justify your answer.
questions.a: False. Science is a process of inquiry, not just a list of names. Memorizing names does not help you understand how the world works; the actual "doing" (observing, guessing, testing) is what makes it science.

questions.q: Think of a kitchen activity, like boiling milk. Can you describe how two different branches of science could explain what is happening?
questions.a: A good answer would explain: 1) Physics (the heat energy from the stove moving into the milk) and 2) Chemistry (the changing properties of milk proteins as they heat up). A poor answer only names one branch without explaining the "why."
